content.user_title: Manage Google Tasks from Your AI Assistant
content.value_statement: Managing Google Tasks through an API requires accurate resource names, methods, parameters, and identifiers. This skill guides Google Workspace CLI operations for lists and tasks.
actual_capabilities: Lists, retrieves, creates, updates, and deletes Google Tasks task lists.
Lists, retrieves, creates, updates, moves, and deletes individual tasks.
Clears completed tasks from a selected task list.
Supports task hierarchy and positioning through the move method.
Guides method discovery with CLI help and schema inspection commands.
limitations: Requires the gws CLI, valid Google authentication, and access to the Google Tasks API.
Does not provide authentication details without the separate gws-shared prerequisite skill.
Cannot create tasks assigned from Google Docs or Chat Spaces through the Tasks API.
Destructive methods can remove related assigned tasks and require careful confirmation.

use_cases.title: Organize Personal Work
use_cases.description: Create task lists, add tasks, and reorder priorities from a conversational workflow.

use_cases.title: Maintain Team Checklists
use_cases.description: Inspect and update shared operational task data with explicit list and task identifiers.

use_cases.title: Automate Task Administration
use_cases.description: Discover CLI schemas and prepare repeatable commands for task list maintenance.

prompt_templates.title: List My Task Lists
prompt_templates.prompt: Show all Google Tasks lists available to my authenticated account. Present each title and identifier before suggesting any changes.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Task
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a task named [task title] in task list [list identifier], due on [date]. Confirm the details before execution.

prompt_templates.title: Reorganize Tasks
prompt_templates.prompt: List tasks in [list identifier], then move [task identifier] under [parent task identifier] at the requested position. Confirm before changing data.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Safe Cleanup
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect [list identifier], identify completed tasks, explain the effect of clearing them, and request confirmation before running any destructive method.

output_examples.input: Move the budget review task under Quarterly Planning.
output_examples.output: The task is ready to move under Quarterly Planning. Confirm the destination list and parent task before applying the change.

output_examples.input: Clear completed tasks from my Work list.
output_examples.output: Clearing hides all completed tasks in the Work list. Confirmation is required before this destructive operation.

best_practices: Run help and schema inspection before using an unfamiliar resource method.
Verify task list and task identifiers before updates, moves, clears, or deletions.
Request explicit confirmation before every destructive operation.
anti_patterns: Do not guess resource identifiers or required method parameters.
Do not delete lists or tasks without explaining related assignment effects.
Do not expose authentication data or include credentials in prompts.

faq.question: What software does this skill require?
faq.answer: It requires the gws CLI, Google authentication, and access to the Google Tasks API.

faq.question: Can it create and update task lists?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents list, get, insert, patch, update, and delete methods for task lists.

faq.question: Can it manage individual tasks?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports listing, retrieving, creating, updating, moving, clearing, and deleting tasks.

faq.question: Does it support subtasks?
faq.answer: Yes. The move method can place a task under a parent and adjust its sibling position.

faq.question: Can it manage tasks assigned from Docs or Chat Spaces?
faq.answer: It can retrieve assigned tasks with suitable options, but the Tasks API cannot create those assignments.

faq.question: How are destructive actions handled?
faq.answer: Users should review affected identifiers and assignment effects, then explicitly confirm clears or deletions before execution.
